transcript:
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Lakshmi Singh.
The president of Iran says his country is still ready to follow through with a proposed
seven-day plan that it presented to the United States.
It's aimed at reopening the Strait of Hormuz.
NPR's Hadil Al-Shalchi reports President Trump rejected the proposal on Saturday.
In an interview with CBS's Face the Nation that aired on Sunday, Masoud Pezashqian said
that after the seven-day milestone and once mutual blockades are lifted, Iran was willing
to sit down for broader talks to formally end military conflict and address its nuclear
program.
In the interview, Pezashqian said that Iran does not seek to develop nuclear weapons and
defended its civilian nuclear program.
Pezashqian also addressed the lack of public appearances by the new supreme leader following
US-Israeli strikes that killed his father.
The Iranian president said he had met the new leader twice and that he was healthy.
President Trump said on Saturday that he rejected Iran's seven-day proposal but that he was
still open to negotiating.
Hadil Al-Shalchi, NPR News, Istanbul.
The Trump administration is now seven months into its war with Iran.
The president may have lost his latest court battle against media organizations he frequently
criticizes.
However, he continued to retaliate by blocking CNN from boarding Air Force One over the weekend
as Trump traveled to a football game in Tennessee.
NPR's Mara Lyasson reports on what Trump standoff with members of the press may or may not be
costing him.
Picking fights with the media might be popular with his base, but it's similar to another
big question that hangs over Trump, which is why is he taking stands that are opposed
to majority public opinion on issue after issue?
The public wants AI regulated, Donald Trump says he doesn't want regulations.
The public is skeptical about data centers.
He said the only people who oppose them are people who want to be quote "poor and backwards."
He's of course four tariffs on the war in Iran, two very, very unpopular policies.
And all of this does not seem to be adding up to a coherent strategy to help his party
win the midterms.
NPR's Mara Lyasson.
A journalist on Nantucket Island came across wooden remnants from what may have been the
19th century Warren Sawyer shipwreck.
It was uncovered during the nor'easter that pummeled Massachusetts and several other states
over the weekend.
In New York, Ocean State Media's David Wright has more on the storm's impact.
The nor'easter walloped the region with heavy rains and winds clocked as high as 70 miles
per hour in New York City.
One Brooklyn man who worked for the city housing authority was struck and killed by a falling
tree.
In some towns on the Jersey Shore, the water was waist deep.
At the height of the storm, 180,000 customers in New Jersey alone lost power.
Work crews were busy all weekend long, and most of the outages have been restored.
It's NPR News.
SpaceX has launched its Starship.
It delivered the most advanced star links yet.
The trip almost did not happen after one of Starship's engines shut down too soon.
However, flight controllers decided to go forward with the mission.
Elon Musk's company had scheduled a 10-hour flight.
However, the company cut short that flight, the spacecraft re-entered Earth's atmosphere
over the Pacific today and splashed down near Hawaii.
The Trump administration is rolling back fuel efficiency standards for new cars.
The rule released today will require that car makers achieve an average of 34.9 miles
of the gallon across their fleets by model year 2031.
Researchers in Canada have discovered two new species that are related to spiders.
Two new species of sea spiders have been discovered by researchers at the University of British
Columbia in Canada.
They were found in the Salish Sea between Washington State and the Canadian province
of British Columbia.
One of the new sea spider species has red eyes and hairy legs.
Cormac Tolar Scott, who led the research that discovered the new species, says they won't
appear crawling across your living room floor.
"They have a hard time on land, they really need to be in the water.
They're quite slow moving, they just kind of crawl on the sea floor."
Scientists have discovered more than 1,300 species of sea spiders.
While the new species are related to spiders, they are also different.
They don't have venom or fangs and mainly rely on camouflage to defend themselves.
Chantalice Duster, NPR News, I'm Lakshmi Singh, NPR News.

Trump administration seven months into war with Iran; Trump blocks CNN from Air Force One

SpaceX launches Starship with advanced Starlinks; spacecraft splashes down near Hawaii after shortened flight
